messages:
jordan: Heads-up — we had a nasty spot outage this morning in us-west-2 (AZ a). All p4d spot capacity evaporated for ~90m, queue latency spiked and a couple of critical batches timed out. Not a full outage but enough to blow past SLOs. Logs attached to the ticket.
sasha: ugh. Any idea whether it was price spikes or capacity reclamation? :thinking_face:
jordan: initial look: AWS reports capacity shortage / no spare p4d in that AZ. Price didn't spike much, so seems capacity-driven. We lost about 60 nodes via spot termination events in quick succession.
lee: sounds like allocation strategy needs revisiting. Price-optimized can be cheap but brittle. We should bias towards capacity-optimized allocation and diversify instance types (mix p4d + p4de + g5 + p3) with weighting.
maria: agreed. Short playbook idea:
1) switch primary spot pools to capacity-optimized (per-request allocation strategy)
2) create heterogenous pools with at least 3 instance families per workload
3) reserve small on-demand warm pool for critical model-serving (5% or min 3 nodes)
4) improve interruption handling: immediate pod eviction -> checkpoint -> requeue to durable queue
5) run chaos test in staging for AZ loss
lee: + add launch-template level settings to prefer AZ spread (placement group tweaks) and set instance weights in autoscaler so multi-type fires predictably.
maria: here's a snippet for the AWS request config we're proposing:
```hcl
placement_strategy = "capacity-optimized"
instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge","p4de.24xlarge","g5.48xlarge","p3dn.24xlarge"]
min_on_demand = 3
spot_percentage = 95
```
jordan: nice. Also we should avoid overbidding. Price-optimized + aggressive bid increases reduces terminations but costs spike. For us: capacity-optimized + broad diversification gives best uptime/cost tradeoff.
kai: interruption handling notes: we need a fast lifecycle-hook that marks node unschedulable, triggers immediate state save for long-running workloads, and uses a short-graceful-drain (~60s) to let RL checkpoint. We should also publish a library/middleware for our model SDK to persist KV caches on preempt.
sasha: ops question — how do we test this without risking prod? Proposal: create a shadow fleet in staging with same allocation strategy and run a scripted AZ eviction (AWS spot interruption simulation or taint nodes). Monitor queue latency.
deploy-bot: incident-ticket #INC-6821 created: "spot capacity spike us-west-2a — followup: allocation strategy review" assigned to @lee @sasha
lee: action items:
- experiment: switch staging pool to capacity-optimized + diversify types (lee)
- add a min-on-demand warm pool for critical serving group (sasha)
- build interruption handler checklist + SDK hooks (kai)
- run AZ eviction test and collect metrics (maria)
Due: 3d
maria: metrics to capture: time-to-recover (tokens/s), queue length, 95th/99th latency, cost delta, % of requests falling back to dedicated.
jordan: if the experiment looks good, roll to canary prod with traffic shifting 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on latency regressions.
sasha: small nit: ensure autoscaler respects instance weights. We had a case where cluster-autoscaler picked many small instances and increased fragmentation.
kai: noted. We'll add tuning flags: prefer larger instance types for heavy models (weight multipliers), and set scale-up-stabilization to 30s.
ops-bot: reminder: next maintenance window 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC for infra changes
jordan: thanks everyone. I'll draft the RFC/playbook this afternoon with the snippets above and the staged rollout plan. :thumbsup:
sasha: ack. I'll pair with lee on the staging run.
lee: starting the staging config change in ~30m, will post results here.
maria: thanks — please paste test dashboard link when ready.
end of thread
